_comment: THE SERVICE AND ENVIRONMENT CATALOG, as a repository declaration.
Program 3 names a 'service/environment catalog' among its nine elements. It
existed as PROSE in the Program 0 release-truth inventory and as frozen JSON
contracts under control-room/contracts/, and as zero rows anywhere. This file
is the declaration; tools/ops-record.py --sync-registry applies it into
ops.service and ops.service_environment. Never hand-edit those tables: the
repo is the source and the database is the render, which is the same posture
every other registry in this system takes.
WHY environment IS 'production' FOR JOBS THAT RUN ON JOE'S MAC. The launchd
jobs are local edge agents by the BDUF's definition, but every one of them
reads and writes the PRODUCTION record layer. The environment field answers
'what was affected', not 'what machine was it typed on' — a Control Room
asking which environment last night's export damaged wants the first answer.
The machine is carried by runtime instead.
CADENCE IS WHAT MAKES SILENCE DETECTABLE, so every scheduled service declares
one, and the grace is sized to the real schedule rather than to the ideal:
rules-refresh runs hourly between 07:00 and 20:00, so its true worst-case gap
is the ELEVEN HOURS overnight, and a 3600s cadence would read stale every
morning by design. local-briefs runs weekdays only and its grace spans the
weekend stand-down, the same lesson tools/health-check.py already learned the
expensive way. A cadence that cries wolf nightly is worse than none: it
trains people to stop reading alarms.
A SERVICE WITH NO CADENCE IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. carr-mcp is not scheduled, so
nothing about it goes stale on a clock; its health comes from synthetic
golden-workflow checks, and until those run it reads unknown — which is the
honest answer for a service nobody has observed.
_comment_scheduled_tasks: THE CLAUDE CODE SCHEDULED TASKS (Program 3, 2026-08-14), registered below
the launchd services. One service per task, keyed IDENTICALLY to the
task's own directory name under ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/<key>/SKILL.md
(that is also the taskId the scheduler reports and the name the launch
marker in each session's own transcript carries) — no separate mapping
table exists to fall out of sync with either. runtime is
'claude-code-scheduled-task': these are prompts a Claude session executes,
not a script with an exit code, so hooks/scheduled-run-record.py (a Stop
hook) derives the outcome from the session's own transcript
deterministically and records it here — see lib/scheduled_run.py.
nightly-record-layer (above, under the launchd services) already exists as
a service for the launchd chain bin/nightly.sh runs; it is NOT duplicated
here. The Claude session that LAUNCHES that chain is recorded under that
SAME service but the fixed run_key 'scheduled-session' (see
lib/scheduled_run.py RUN_KEY), distinct from the chain's own 'nightly.*'
step keys, so the two can never collide.
ONLY THE CURRENTLY-ENABLED TASKS ARE REGISTERED. x-reply-run-daily,
linkedin-engagement-daily and calendar-fetch-daily are disabled
(`list_scheduled_tasks`, checked 2026-08-14) and deliberately left
unregistered: a cadence-bound service for a task nobody is running would
read STALE forever, which is exactly the false-alarm failure mode
local-briefs' grace design and the launchd services above already learned
to avoid. Register one when its task is re-enabled — sync-registry retires
a service that leaves this file, never the reverse, so nothing is lost by
waiting.
CADENCE for the weekly tasks uses the SAME 604800s/172800s (7 day cadence,
2 day grace) local-briefs already established for a task that can miss its
one weekly window if the Mac is asleep; the monthly tasks (which actually
fire once inside a several-day window via their own internal ledger gate,
per each SKILL.md) use 2592000s/518400s so the window itself is not
mistaken for drift.

services.name: CARR record and doctrine API (Cloudflare Worker)
services.purpose: Every record verb, the doctrine store, the Deal Room web host, and OAuth.

services.name: Neon Postgres record layer
services.purpose: The canonical store. Every verb, generator, exporter and retrieval stops without it.

services.name: Nightly record-layer chain
services.purpose: Cadence, matcher, exports, corpus push, consumers, graph, backup — in that order.

environments.notes: Daily at 02:05. Two hours of grace covers a long backup.

services.name: Taught-rule refresh
services.purpose: Re-renders the compiled rule files Dell's sessions boot from.

environments.notes: Hourly 07:00-20:00 by fourteen calendar entries, so the real worst-case gap is the eleven hours overnight — not one hour.

services.name: Local brief pack and review queue
services.purpose: Rebuilds brief-pack and review-queue every business morning.

environments.notes: Weekdays 06:45. The grace spans the weekend stand-down; weekends are off for both partners.

services.name: Apple Notes capture sweep
services.purpose: Pulls new notes into the capture queue.

services.name: Partner interrupt channel
services.purpose: The Joe/Dell interrupt poll.

environments.notes: Wakes every two minutes, but bin/run-scheduled.sh's --heartbeat-interval (Program 4 follow-up) throttles a SUCCEEDED row to at most one per 1800s — recording all ~720 fires/day as rows would be pure noise from a healthy channel. Every FAILURE is still recorded immediately regardless of the throttle, so cadence here reflects the succeeded heartbeat, not the wake. This job once logged 382 consecutive identical 'nothing new' lines to a local log with a broken query, because a channel with nothing to say and a channel that cannot ask produce byte-identical output — a run row (even throttled) still distinguishes them, since a genuinely broken query fails loud and is recorded on the spot.

services.name: Capture queue poll
services.purpose: Drains the capture inbox.

environments.notes: Wakes every 5 min, but bin/run-scheduled.sh's --heartbeat-interval (Program 4 follow-up) throttles a SUCCEEDED row to at most one per 1800s (30 min) — recording all ~288 fires/day would be noise from a quiet inbox. Every FAILURE is still recorded immediately regardless of the throttle.

services.name: Calendar EventKit capture
services.purpose: Local, attendee-aware calendar read (EventKit) into stamp-touch, replacing the published feed the Cowork calendar-fetch-daily task read (which Microsoft strips attendees from). Weekdays 07:20. See ops/launchd/com.carr.calendar-eventkit.plist's own header for the PROP-010 ruling this job exists under.

environments.notes: Weekdays at 07:20 only. Grace spans the weekend stand-down (Joe, 2026-07-11), same shape as local-briefs: the real worst-case gap is Friday to Monday, not one day. PR #97 (Program 4 slice 1) wired the other six launchd jobs and deliberately left this one out for lack of a registration; this entry and the plist's own routing through bin/run-scheduled.sh close that gap.

services.name: Joe's Mac — local edge node presence
services.purpose: The registered fact of this Mac's own presence, per PROP-010 (deterministic recurring work runs from versioned repo code executed by a registered Local Edge Node through launchd). Not a job's business outcome — a heartbeat that this machine is awake, Joe is logged in, and launchd is actually waking its agents. A sleeping, logged-out, FileVault-locked, or otherwise unreachable Mac must read stale or unknown here, never healthy.

environments.notes: Recorded by bin/run-scheduled.sh's --also-heartbeat flag, riding partner-ping's own 2-minute launchd wake as an independent second provenance line (key=launchd.heartbeat), throttled to at most one succeeded row per 1800s by the SAME --heartbeat-interval — regardless of whether the partner-ping buzz query itself succeeds. A Mac that is asleep or logged out stops waking the LaunchAgent at all, so this service goes stale within 2700s (45 min) of the last real wake rather than reading healthy on a stopped clock.

services.name: Claude Code version sentinel
services.purpose: Watches for a Claude Code release that changes hook or settings behaviour.

services.name: Recording retention purge
services.purpose: Deletes call recordings past their retention window.

services.name: Weekly NPI new-provider sweep
services.purpose: NPPES weekly file to territory lead digest and hot-leads dashboard.

services.name: Weekly social analytics pull
services.purpose: Pulls X/FB/IG/LinkedIn metrics and records them via measure-placement.

services.name: Friday social batch
services.purpose: Drafts + graphics for the following week, queued to Blotato as review-drafts.

services.name: Monthly system health audit
services.purpose: Re-scores the 12-category report card and appends a trend column.

environments.deploy_mechanism: Claude Code scheduled task (native), cron 0 9 6-10 * * (fires daily in-window; the task's own ledger gate runs it once per month)

services.name: Monthly idea-bank resurface
services.purpose: Resurfaces idea-bank entries worth another look.

environments.deploy_mechanism: Claude Code scheduled task (native), cron 0 9 5-11 * * (fires daily in-window; the task's own ledger gate runs it once per month)

services.name: Monthly size/prune sweep
services.purpose: Prunes bloat ahead of the playbook review.

environments.deploy_mechanism: Claude Code scheduled task (native), cron 30 8 15-21 * * (fires daily in-window; the task's own ledger gate runs it once per month)

services.name: Monthly playbook review
services.purpose: Reviews the playbooks after the size sweep.

environments.deploy_mechanism: Claude Code scheduled task (native), cron 0 9 15-21 * * (fires daily in-window; the task's own ledger gate runs it once per month)

services.name: Weekly contact enrichment slice
services.purpose: Open-source contact enrichment, 40 records/run until the book is covered.

services.name: Weekly deal-history counterparty research
services.purpose: Open-source research on Salesforce deal-history counterparties, 25 records/run.

services.name: Weekly backup restore rehearsal
services.purpose: Proves the encrypted backups actually restore; PASS/FAIL against production row counts.

environments.deploy_mechanism: Claude Code scheduled task (native), cron 40 7 * * 2 (runs bin/restore-rehearse.sh)

services.name: Weekly Claude Code update audit
services.purpose: On a Claude Code version change, audits what the release changes for CARR.

services.name: Weekday loop drain
services.purpose: Works the claude-owned loop queue and closes loops by doing the work.

environments.notes: Weekdays only; the grace spans the weekend stand-down, same as local-briefs.

services.name: Weekly Radar digest
services.purpose: Scores the week's lead candidates across all lanes and carries lead-system maintenance.

services.name: Logitech modifier-key repair
services.purpose: Re-applies the hidutil modifier mapping, which dies on reboot and on receiver replug.

environments.notes: Wakes every 10 min and is idempotent by design, so a missed pass costs a keyboard that behaves oddly until the next one. The cadence is deliberately 2h rather than 10 min, with run-scheduled.sh's heartbeat throttle doing the same job it does for capture-poll: recording 144 identical successes a day would be noise, and a low-criticality cosmetic repair does not earn a row that goes stale within the hour.

services.name: Record-derived egress host allowlist
services.purpose: Regenerates the machine-local host allowlist so the egress guard does not silently fall back to the code list.

environments.notes: NO CADENCE ON PURPOSE, and this one is not a scheduled job that happens to lack a schedule. The plist is SECONDARY MACHINE ONLY: on Joe's primary Mac the allowlist is regenerated as a step of the nightly chain, so this agent is deliberately not installed here and a cadence would report it missing every single day on the one machine where its absence is correct. It is registered so the service EXISTS in the catalog for the machines that do run it.

services.name: Call-mode dictation server
services.purpose: Long-running server backing meeting capture; holds the recording session state.

environments.notes: KeepAlive server, so the health question is 'is it up' and never 'did it fire recently'. bin/probe-keepalive.py answers it every 10 min by opening a TCP connection to 127.0.0.1:4682 — a connect proves it is ACCEPTING, which is a real answer rather than a PID sighting. Still exempt from bin/run-scheduled.sh: the wrapper records on child exit, and a KeepAlive child exiting means launchd restarted it. The 30-minute cadence means one missed probe pass is not an alarm.

services.name: Doc conversation server
services.purpose: Long-running local server for the Doc conversational surface.

environments.notes: KeepAlive server. Probed every 10 min by a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:4680, which proves it is ACCEPTING rather than merely running. Same wrapper exemption and the same reason as call-mode. Proven end to end on 2026-08-14: stopping the agent produced SEV-3 INC-20260814-08 within one probe pass, and restarting it moved the incident to monitoring.

services.name: Desk dictation agent
services.purpose: Phase B desk dictation, distinct from meeting-mode consent capture.

environments.notes: KeepAlive server with NO PORT TO KNOCK ON, so its probe is process liveness only — a weaker claim than the other two, and the run detail says which signal was used so the row is never read as more than it is. A wedged process and a healthy one both have a PID. Same wrapper exemption and reason as call-mode.

services.name: Recording capture bridge, claim side
services.purpose: Claims new recording sessions as they appear under ~/Recordings.

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered, so SILENCE IS THE NORMAL STATE — it fires only when a recording session starts. Any cadence would cry wolf on every day Joe records nothing, which is most days, and an alarm that fires on a quiet day is how both partners learn to stop reading alarms.

services.name: Recording consent announcer
services.purpose: Plays the all-party consent announcement when a recording session begins.

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered; silence is normal, so no cadence. Criticality is HIGH despite being a small watcher: it is what makes the rig announce recording aloud, and Florida is an all-party-consent state. A failure here is a legal exposure rather than an inconvenience, which is why it is registered even though nothing can currently observe it firing.

services.name: Video encode watcher
services.purpose: Encodes video dropped into the CARR Video Pipeline intake folder.

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered; silence is normal, so no cadence. Its script lives OUTSIDE the repo, under ~/Movies, which means it is not version-controlled and would not survive the Mac — worth naming here because the catalog is where that kind of exposure becomes visible.

services.name: KeepAlive server liveness probe
services.purpose: Asks the three long-running servers whether they are up, and writes the answer to the ledger.

environments.notes: Wakes every 10 min; cadence declared at 30 min so one missed pass is not an alarm. It is itself wrapped by bin/run-scheduled.sh, because a watcher whose own failure is invisible is the one thing nothing watches. It returns EX_CONFIG (78) rather than a failure when NOTHING could be recorded at all, since three records failing on one pass is an unreachable ledger rather than three simultaneous outages — and a probe that alarmed every 10 minutes on a Mac whose credential had not loaded would be the smoke-suite mistake again.
